items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 18 at 3:24AM EDT until October 19 at 11:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement,
strong longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...West Carteret County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to 11
AM EDT Monday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Sunday
morning through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some roads and low
lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes
adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow flooding.
Strong longshore currents will create dangerous swimming
conditions.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

items.headline: Gale Warning issued October 18 at 2:43AM EDT until October 20 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...North winds 25 to 35 kt with occasional gusts up to 50
kt and seas 13 to 18 ft.

* WHERE...The coastal waters from Ocracoke Inlet to Surf City,
and the offshore waters from Cape Lookout to Surf City.

* WHEN...Until 8 AM EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.
